title: Bouchées de plantains aux crevettes (Plantain and Prawn Rolls)
author: Darlene (International Cuisine)
desc: Raw peeled prawns wrapped in thin lengthwise strips of plantain, secured with toothpicks and fried until golden and cooked through, served with a chilled tomato, spring-onion and lemon sauce.
longDesc: An appetiser from the International Cuisine site, labelled Cameroon. Tomatoes, spring onions, yellow bell pepper, lemon juice, ginger, salt and pepper are mixed and chilled. The prawns are salted. The plantains are sliced lengthwise into long thin strips and each prawn wrapped and secured with a toothpick, then fried until golden brown all over and cooked through. Drained and served with the chilled sauce. The author notes the plantain wraps tended to break and that the result ‘did not end up as rolls’.
ingredients: 1 bunch of spring onions, finely chopped
1 small yellow bell pepper, de-seeded and finely diced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: Mix the tomatoes, spring onions, bell pepper, lemon juice, ginger, salt and pepper and chill.
Slice the plantains lengthwise into long, thin strips.
Wrap each prawn in a strip and secure with a toothpick.
Fry until golden brown all over and cooked through. Drain and serve with the chilled sauce.
chefTips: The printed doneness cue is ‘golden brown all over and cooked through’.
The author found the plantain wraps tended to break.
The ripeness of the plantain is not printed.
commonMistakes: Cutting the plantain strips too thick or thin.
Frying in oil that is not hot enough.
healthBenefits: Prawns give lean protein; the plantain strips add starch and the frying adds oil.
culturalNote: The page labels the dish Cameroon; the author describes it as ‘another lovely recipe from Cameroon’ and says it did not turn out as rolls.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Cameroon Plantain and Prawn Rolls’ (card: ‘Bouchées de Plantains aux Crevettes’). Byline: ‘Darlene at International Cuisine’ in metadata; the recipe card says ‘International Cuisine’ (site name). Published 2014-11-20, modified 2026-05-19 (metadata only). Yield 4.
